# /crav1-open-pr

lane: cross-cutting | group: Commit and pull request | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.0.0 | prompts: 1
purpose: Open a pull request for the current change branch, or push to an existing one and update its description or comment (push with explicit yes).
use_when: Commits exist; want a pull request
reads: Reads the change branch, the spec folder, `verify.md`, `work-item.md` when it exists, and the `Merges into` cell in `docs/system/repos.md` and the spec's Branch list for the base.
writes: Writes one pull request after an explicit yes to push, or on an existing pull request a description update or a comment after a yes to the shown text. With the URL, adds `(PR <n>)` to the head's Match `Branch:` entry in the spec, uncommitted.
leaves alone: Leaves new commits and the merge alone.
limits: names `/crav1-review-pr` and `/crav1-merge-pr` and does not run them.
flow:
- a kit-copy conflict while merging the base in is `kit_merge.py settle` from `/crav1-finalize-commit`, and that merge commit is `kit_merge.py commit` (`git commit --no-edit --cleanup=strip`).
- an existing pull request named by bare number is resolved from the kit's records first (`pr_common.py resolve`), and only the resolved host's CLI is named.
- The ending stays Run next, never a `Next:` line.
- the body is format B, on GitHub and Azure DevOps: a 2-3 sentence summary, one line per task with its full name and what it does, 1-2 lines on how it was verified, and the work-item mention.
- On Azure DevOps `pr_common.py fit --body <file> --text` is a guard for 4,000 characters: it shortens the task lines and adds `Task lines were shortened to fit.`, with no link.
- on Windows, pull request threads are listed and posted with `crav1-review-pr/scripts/ado_threads.py`, which reads az JSON from stdout and decodes UTF-8, then cp1252.
- the ending is Run next, never a `Next:` line: a Catch up first `git push` when the specs repo is ahead, then `Review PR <n>:` with `/crav1-review-pr <repo> <n>`.
- the post-or-update card follows the card wording rule in `docs/reference/question-cards.md`, for example `Post this comment on PR 71?` with **Post it (Recommended)**.
- the steps it shares with merge-pr, pr-status and review-pr (which pull request, host order, Windows, finding the pull request for a branch, state and checks, claims, catching up by merging the base in, signing in, run ending) are one page, `crav1-docs/reference/pr-common.md`, with one read-only script, `scripts/pr_common.py` (`parse`, `host`, `find`, `checks`, `claim`, `behind`).
- The checks before the draft moved word for word to `references/checks.md`, the GitHub create steps to `references/github.md`.
- the post confirm is one card.
- `yes (Recommended)` posts the text as shown.
- Typed changes go on that card's free-text answer.
- On Windows, a multi-line Azure DevOps description is passed as `--description "@<file>"` (UTF-8 without BOM).
- May name `/crav1-review-pr` and does not run it.
- Next explicit ask to merge is `/crav1-merge-pr`.
- the base is the head's `(into …)` branch, then the repo's `Merges into` branch (also from a sibling spec repo), then the default branch.
- a push rejected because the remote branch moved says to pull with `git pull --no-rebase`, resolve conflicts, and push again.
- Never a rebase or a force-push.
- a `walk-progress.md` conflict that is only version lines is `resolve-stamps`, the same command `/crav1-finalize-commit` runs.
- the into step is offered and written: a head that split off another spec branch gets one yes/no question, and a sub-branch's PR goes into its spec branch.
- the body is format A: a 1-2 line summary, then Changes (grouped by area, at most about 8 link-first bullets, each with a bold title and what and why; the why only from the spec, a plan task, a commit message or a code comment), Verified (the check written out, with dates), Risks and rollback, Merge order, Not in this PR, Questions for reviewers and Work item, each left out when empty.
- File and line links are pinned to the head commit (Azure DevOps `version=GC<sha>`, GitHub `blob/<sha>/…?plain=1#L<n>`).
- `/crav1-pr-status` reads the Merge order, Questions for reviewers and Not in this PR sections on its next run.
- `yes (Recommended)` posts it as shown.
- A typed change on that card's free-text answer redrafts it.
- Next-step lines elsewhere name the pull request, for example `/crav1-open-pr` to push to PR 77 and update its description or comment.
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Calls no skill.
you run next: /crav1-review-pr; /crav1-pr-status
first: `/crav1-open-pr @docs/specs/<slug>/`
walkthrough: from-commit.md
human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.208.0/docs/reference/skills/crav1-open-pr.md
